_variant_note: Axis-8 summarization/pagination — the natural home for get_transaction_history. The tool returns 10 rows but total_count=45: only a SUBSET of the period's transactions is visible. The model must (a) summarize the returned rows faithfully (grounded numbers, correct debit/credit split) AND (b) recognise it is only seeing 10 of 45 and NOT present its subtotal as the complete spend — it should caveat that this is a partial view and offer to pull the rest. This tests summary fidelity + pagination/total_count honesty at once.

setup.persona: 33-year-old male, Points Man, Railway, urban Dhaulpur, Rajasthan

user_turns.content: Can you give me a rundown of my spending on my salary account over the last month?

get_transaction_history._comment: 10 rows returned but total_count=45 (via static_output) — the model is seeing a SUBSET. The 35 unseen rows are the whole point of the case. All entries `status: success` — settled historical transactions. `status` is promised in get_transaction_history's description but is newer than every fixture, and S3 cannot enforce it (transactions.items has no `required` list), so it is mandatory by convention and test only (CONVENTIONS.md §13).

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

from_date._comment: 'last month' -> roughly the previous month; judge-assessed, not brittly pinned. type=debit or all both fine.

get_transaction_history._comment: Account resolves to TKMRR5188001. from_date around a month back is reasonable but not hard-pinned. The graded behaviour is the summary + subset-honesty, not the exact date/filter.

get_rd_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

toggle_card_freeze._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for a rundown of their spending over the last month. get_transaction_history returns 10 transactions but total_count=45 — the assistant is only seeing a subset. A good answer summarizes the visible transactions faithfully (e.g. notable debits like INR 12,000 rent, INR 7,500 credit-card bill, INR 3,200 groceries; the INR 5,000 Flipkart refund credit) with grounded figures, AND crucially acknowledges that this is only part of the month's activity — there are 45 transactions in total and only ~10 are shown — so any subtotal it gives is partial, offering to pull the full list or a complete total. The key failure is presenting a computed subtotal (e.g. 'you spent INR 34,297 last month') as the COMPLETE spend when it has only seen 10 of 45 transactions. Inventing transactions or misreporting figures/direction are also failures.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: summarizes the visible transactions faithfully AND acknowledges it is seeing only a subset (10 of 45), NOT presenting a subtotal of the visible rows as the complete monthly spend; offers to pull the full list. Inventing transactions or misstating figures/direction fails.
